messages:
maria: Heads-up — overnight backfills in us-west2 triggered intermittent 0.5-3% packet loss between GPU nodes. Seen across two different racks, bursts last ~10-30s and line up with heavy checkpoint shipping.

josh: ack. any obvious MTU/GSO/GRO mismatch? can you paste `ip link` + `ethtool -k` from one affected node?

maria: pasted below from node gpu-usw2-03 (affected):
```
$ ip link show vxlan0
3: vxlan0@if2: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether d6:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
```
```
$ ethtool -k eth0
Generic-offload: on
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
gso: on
gro: on
```

maria: also ran a quick tcpdump during a burst — see many retransmits and a few ICMP frag needed messages even though MTU is 1450 on overlay and 9000 on host.

ken: that MTU mismatch on overlay vs host is normal. more interesting: are we seeing any driver regressions? which kernel/driver versions on affected hosts?

maria: nodes show `5.19.16-rt` on rack A, `5.15.0` on rack B (we're mid-rolling kernels last week).

shanice: ugh, mixed kernels could explain non-deterministic offload behavior. recent note: mlx5 driver had a GSO/GRO regression on 5.19 in our vendor patch set. can you run `cat /sys/class/net/eth0/features` and check `dmesg | grep -i mlx\n`?

maria: quick outputs:
```
$ cat /sys/class/net/eth0/features
rx-checksumming tx-checksumming scatter-gather tcp-segmentation-offload tx-checksum-ip-generic
rx-vlan-hw-offload hw-tc-offload
```
```
$ dmesg | tail -n 30
mlx5: module version 5.16.0 vendor 2.3.1 loaded
mlx5_core: Mellanox ConnectX-6 detected
mlx5_core: SR-IOV enabled, 2 VFs configured
```

josh: any RDMA traffic on these jobs? sometimes RDMA driver paths override kernel offload heuristics.

maria: checkpoints use high-throughput scatter uploads (grpc over tcp), no explicit RDMA, but some infra tests enable RDMA for other fleets on same hosts.

ken: also check softnet stats while a burst is happening: `cat /proc/net/softnet_stat | awk '{print $1" "$2" "$3}' | head` — look for high drops (column 3 indicates dropped pkts).

maria: ran that during a burst, column 3 jumped into the 10k-20k range in 20s window on one of the hosts.

shanice: that points to software congestion (softnet backlog) rather than pure wire loss. could be CPU steal or IRQ affinity issues. are CPU loads spiking during bursts?

maria: yes, %steal and irq/softirq counters spike on the affected host when the backfill runs.

ken: possible culprit: co-located daemon that changes RPS/XPS or moves IRQs when backfill starts (e.g., a node-level uploader). can you capture `irqbalance` status + `cat /proc/interrupts` before/during/after?

maria: captured interrupts — during burst we see huge increase on eth0 rx queue interrupts on cpu0 and very little on other cpus. irqbalance is enabled but pinned to cpuset for system tasks.

josh: next steps suggestion: 1) replicate burst on a single host by running iperf UDP/TCP with similar flow count, 2) force IRQ affinity to spread RX queues across cores, 3) temporarily disable GSO/GRO on vxlan interface to see if retransmits drop.

maria: starting iperf run now on a test node, will toggle `ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off` and report.

deploy-bot: auto-alert — packet-drop-rate/us-west2/gpu-pool exceeded threshold (1%) at 2026-03-09T00:12:40Z, alert-id a1f4e

maria: quick experiment results: disabling GSO/GRO reduced retransmits and softnet drops dropped to low hundreds, but CPU usage increased ~12% on that node. latency tail improved.

shanice: that confirms offload interaction. disabling is not ideal for production due to CPU cost. we should: a) pin IRQs correctly for RX queues, b) ensure consistent kernel/driver across racks, c) test vendor mlx5 firmware rollback/upgrade for the GSO regression, d) consider adjusting backfill rate limiter to avoid saturating single NIC queues.

ken: +1. also check cni tunnel implementation — some tunnel code paths copy/slice packets differently when GSO is active. which CNI/kernel encapsulation code do we run?

maria: we're on our custom kube-overlay with Geneve encapsulation (vxlan shim). code path is in userspace dataplane for some hosts (dpdk fallback), kernel on others.

josh: mix of userspace dp and kernel encap + mixed kernels + mlx5 quirks = perfect storm. recommend: isolate a canary pool with uniform kernel/firmware and kernel vxlan dataplane, run backfills for 24h and monitor.

maria: creating canary pool now and throttling backfill concurrency to 6 per host. i'll report back with telemetry after a few cycles.

shanice: thanks — set an incident note and tag eng-sre if the canary sees >0.8% drop again. +document the repro steps so we can file a vendor bug if firmware change needed. :white_check_mark:
